title: Juncadella wins Brands Hatch Race 1 for his first DTM victory
dek: Daniel Juncadella won Saturday’s DTM race at Brands Hatch by 7.896 seconds for Mercedes-AMG after dropping to third at the start, with Farfus second for BMW and Auer third.

chapters.title: A new Grand Prix loop and a weekend squeezed into two days
text: The DTM came to Brands Hatch for the sixth of its ten race weekends, with races 11 and 12 of the 20-race season. It was the series’ first visit to the Kent circuit since 2013 and its first time on the Grand Prix layout, just under four kilometres long, which meant that nobody in the paddock had ever driven a DTM car there.

The calendar made the learning curve steeper. The circuit may use the Grand Prix loop on only a limited number of days, so there was no Friday running: three practice sessions, two qualifying sessions and both races were squeezed into Saturday and Sunday. Mercedes team boss Ulrich Fritz called Brands Hatch the first real unknown of the year, with a much higher risk of a set-up mistake. Gary Paffett described it as a home race for him but not a track he knew well.

Mercedes, in its final DTM season, had won six of the first ten races, against three for BMW and one for Audi, and its drivers Paffett and Paul di Resta ran first and second in the championship. Audi arrived with fresh hope after René Rast’s win at Zandvoort, which came from a lap-one pit stop, although few observers expected that to be repeated. Race 1 followed the usual format: a 55-minute race with one mandatory pit stop for tyres.

chapters.title: Juncadella finds the lap in the final minute
text: Daniel Juncadella took pole position with a 1m18.069s in the last minute of the 20-minute session. Lucas Auer had led going into the final five minutes, ahead of the BMW of Augusto Farfus, who had set the pace in practice, and improved again after Juncadella’s lap but fell 0.092 seconds short. It was an all-Mercedes front row.

René Rast was third on 1m18.255s and the only Audi in the top ten. Philipp Eng was fourth for BMW, just 0.002 seconds behind him, and Farfus slipped to fifth. Gary Paffett had touched the barrier at Paddock Hill early in the session but avoided serious damage and set the sixth-fastest time. Timo Glock spun at Surtees at the very end, which brought out the yellow flags, after he had banked seventh place.

Edoardo Mortara, Marco Wittmann and Pascal Wehrlein completed the top ten, with Wehrlein only 0.001 seconds behind Wittmann. Robin Frijns was the next-best Audi in 11th. Paul di Resta, Paffett’s main title rival, could manage only 12th, and Jamie Green’s struggles at his home track left him 17th, with Bruno Spengler’s BMW last, more than half a second slower than anyone else.

chapters.title: Juncadella bogs down and Rast dives for the pits
text: Juncadella made a poor start and lost two places. Auer took the lead and Rast went round the outside of the polesitter at Paddock Hill Bend and Druids to take second. Behind them Farfus went past his BMW team-mate Eng for fourth on the opening lap.

At the end of that lap several cars dived into the pit lane for the mandatory stop, Rast among them, which handed second place straight back to Juncadella. Loïc Duval, who had also stopped, slid into the gravel at Druids on cold tyres. His Audi was beached, a slow zone was deployed for the first few laps while it was recovered, and his race was over after a single lap. The neutralisation hurt Rast’s plan: the strategy that had worked at Zandvoort did not pay off in the same way here.

chapters.title: Juncadella stops first and overcuts Auer
text: Once the slow zone ended, Farfus and Eng came in, and Paffett followed on lap six. Juncadella stopped at the end of lap seven and came out just ahead of Farfus, while Auer, the net leader, came in soon afterwards. He rejoined on cold tyres and had no answer: within two laps of his own stop Juncadella dived past him at Graham Hill Bend, and Farfus followed him through, leaving the Austrian third.

For a time the real leaders were the Mercedes drivers who had not stopped. Pascal Wehrlein and Edoardo Mortara ran longest of all, with Mortara coming in around lap 11 or 12 and Wehrlein, the last driver to stop, on lap 15. Both rejoined in the middle of the top ten, and the gamble brought them only seventh and eighth at the flag.

chapters.title: Three abreast at Hawthorns
text: With overtaking so hard on the Grand Prix loop, the best action came behind the leaders. Timo Glock and Jamie Green fought side by side for position, and Mike Rockenfeller closed up on the pair before taking both of them at Hawthorns in a move that had three cars running abreast into the corner. Glock, who had complained of heavy understeer, dropped to 13th.
In the closing laps Rockenfeller also got past Robin Frijns to take the last point. Green passed Frijns too on the final lap, but finished 2.4 seconds short of the top ten at his home race.

chapters.title: Juncadella eases clear to win by 7.9 seconds
text: Juncadella pulled steadily clear after taking the lead and crossed the line 7.896 seconds ahead of Farfus after 41 laps and 57m15.601s. It was his first DTM victory and Mercedes’ seventh win of the season. He said he had pushed every lap as in qualifying and only realised late on that the win was safe, taking the last lap calmly and keeping off the kerbs. Fritz praised him for a fantastic performance all day.

Farfus, who had started fifth, made his first podium of the season and his first in the DTM since 2016, and said he was extremely glad to be back on the rostrum. Auer held on for third, 10.040 seconds behind the winner, and said that track position was everything at Brands Hatch. Rast was fourth, 4.7 seconds behind Auer and the best of the Audis, with Rockenfeller the only other one in the top ten.

Eng resisted a late attack from Paffett to take fifth by 0.387 seconds, with Wehrlein, Mortara and Wittmann, who set the fastest lap on lap seven, following. Di Resta, the other title contender, was a subdued 16th of the 17 finishers and left without a point, so Paffett’s lead over him grew to 35 points, 156 to 121, with Auer up to third on 106.

facts.v: Daniel Juncadella won his first DTM race in his 67th start, after taking his first podium at the Norisring a few weeks earlier.
Juncadella’s 1m18.069s in the final minute beat Lucas Auer’s Mercedes by 0.092 seconds and gave Mercedes an all-Mercedes front row.

facts.v: Augusto Farfus climbed from fifth on the grid to second, his first podium of the season and his first since 2016.
Gary Paffett led the standings on 156 points from Paul di Resta on 121, with Lucas Auer third on 106.
